19.description: The committee recommends City Council approve $100,000 in 2026 capital funding for Persephone Theatre, Nutrien Wonderhub, and Broadway Theatre, supporting cultural infrastructure projects.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Mayor Block praised Persephone Theatre's work and the River Landing ecosystem.
Persephone Theatre serves over 50,000 patrons and 800 youth annually.
Persephone Theatre's director advocated for roof replacement funding.

22.description: The committee recommended a new Development Incentives Policy to City Council, aiming to support affordable housing and strategic redevelopment.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
4 for, 0 against
Councillor Jeffries moved to send the report back for more options, sparking debate on process.
Developers, affordable housing projects, and businesses in Riversdale are affected.
Council sought broader incentive eligibility beyond administration's proposed priority growth areas.
The new policy removes vacancy requirements for incentives, encouraging redevelopment.
What are the implications for water and sewer capacity on potential secondary corridors?
Delegates urged expanding incentive eligibility to more areas and maintaining full tax abatements.
New policy enhances tax abatements and off-site levy waivers for affordable housing projects.
Administration will report back on implications of extending incentives to secondary corridors.

18.description: City administration is not recommending allowing secondary suites in dwelling groups at this time, citing existing methods and potential infrastructure challenges.

chips.text: Individual dwelling unit owners can add units through existing permit applications.
Administration will monitor and revisit the issue if conditions change.

24.description: Council reviewed the list of reports requested from city administration, discussing delays on a National Urban Park inquiry and a landscape design report, with updates expected in March and earlier than late 2026.

chips.text: Councillor Glaser questioned the relevance of a 2022 park inquiry.
Relevance of 2022 National Urban Park inquiry remains to be fully addressed.
Administration committed to bringing landscape design report earlier than late 2026.

25.description: The city plans to move the proposed East Side Leisure Centre to an adjacent site in the Holmwood sector. This relocation addresses school safety concerns and keeps the $65 million project on schedule.

chips.text: Relocation won't add costs or delay timelines, potentially speeding construction.
Addresses safety concerns for 3,600 students at two high schools.
Nearly 5,500 participants gave input on desired amenities in 2024.
Administration will advise province of city's support for leisure center relocation.
